value: sum to total variance; interactions shared equally
conditions: T=n.a.; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=n.a.; phase=n.a.; surface=n.a.; inputs=independent inputs
method: computation: analytical results for variance-based sensitivity indices
notes: Iooss and Prieur (arXiv 1707.01334; published Int. J. Uncertainty Quantification 2019, 10.1615/int.j.uncertaintyquantification.2019028372). For independent inputs the Shapley effects sum to the output variance and each interaction effect is apportioned equally to the inputs in it.

value: non-negative, sum to one with correlated inputs
conditions: T=n.a.; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=n.a.; phase=n.a.; surface=n.a.; inputs=dependent (correlated) inputs
method: computation: analytical results for variance-based sensitivity indices
notes: Shapley effects account for both interactions and correlations of an input; consequence printed: they are non negative and sum to one, which allows ranking. Supports the methods sentence that Shapley effects share variance among correlated inputs without assuming independence.

value: equal to Sobol indices without correlation; sandwiched with correlation
conditions: T=n.a.; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=n.a.; phase=n.a.; surface=n.a.; inputs=linear model, Gaussian inputs
method: computation: analytical Shapley effects of a linear Gaussian model
notes: With rho = 0 the Shapley effects equal the first-order and total Sobol indices; with correlation they lie between the full first-order and the independent total indices (the authors' sandwich effect). Supports repeating the Shapley ranking under independence as a check.

value: non-zero effect for a correlated input absent from the model
conditions: T=n.a.; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=n.a.; phase=n.a.; surface=n.a.; inputs=Y = X1 with (X1, X2) correlated Gaussian
notes: An input not involved in the model can receive a non-zero Shapley effect if it is correlated with an influential input; perfectly correlated inputs get equal effects. Matches the reading stated in src/nacre/screen/shapley.py.

value: removes conceptual problems of dependent-input ANOVA indices
conditions: T=n.a.; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=n.a.; phase=n.a.; surface=n.a.; inputs=dependent inputs
method: computation: analytical properties of Shapley value importance
notes: Owen and Prieur (arXiv 1610.02080; published SIAM/ASA J. Uncertainty Quantification 2017, 10.1137/16m1097717). Main goal stated: show that Shapley value removes the conceptual problems of Sobol-type indices when inputs are dependent.

value: bracketed between two Sobol indices (independent inputs)
conditions: T=n.a.; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=n.a.; phase=n.a.; surface=n.a.; inputs=independent inputs
method: compilation: summary of Owen 2014 and Song et al. 2016
notes: States that Owen (2014) derived the Shapley value with variance explained as the value for independent inputs, bracketed between two Sobol indices, and that Song et al. (2016) advocated it for dependent inputs. Secondary statement of TP-007 and TP-008, checked against their abstracts.

conditions: T=n.a.; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=n.a.; phase=n.a.; surface=n.a.; inputs=independent inputs
method: computation: game-theoretic derivation of variance-explained Shapley value
notes: Owen 2014, Sobol' indices and Shapley value (SIAM/ASA JUQ). Abstract only (no open copy): the Shapley value with variance explained matches neither usual Sobol index and is bracketed between them, so Sobol indices give computable bounds.

value: defined for dependent inputs; Monte Carlo estimator
conditions: T=n.a.; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=n.a.; phase=n.a.; surface=n.a.; inputs=dependent inputs
method: computation: Monte Carlo estimation of Shapley effects
notes: Song, Nelson and Staum 2016 (SIAM/ASA JUQ). Abstract only (no open copy): names Owen's measure the Shapley effect, analyses it for dependent inputs, and proposes a Monte Carlo algorithm (the permutation design cited in src/nacre/screen/shapley.py).
